takeaways.title: Quantify the requirement, then size resilience to it
takeaways.body: Turn every NFR into a number with a window (99.95% monthly, p95 under 500 ms, RPO 5 minutes) before choosing services; latency, availability and recoverability are non-functional even when worded as features. If an option adds redundancy beyond the stated target for a low-value or internal workload, the cost optimization pillar makes it wrong. When two designs both meet the target, pick the simpler, more managed, decoupled and stateless one.

takeaways.title: HA is not DR: compare the copy interval to the RPO
takeaways.body: Zone failure is solved by a regional MIG with autohealing and autoscaling behind a load balancer, or Cloud SQL HA; region failure needs data and compute in another region. A nightly backup cannot meet a 5-minute RPO, so use continuous replication, PITR or multi-region Spanner instead of a faster restore. Tier the portfolio: active-active for tier 1, warm standby for tier 2, backup and restore for tier 3, and use immutable backup vaults for ransomware.

takeaways.title: Default to the most managed compute that meets the control need
takeaways.body: New stateless container that should scale to zero is Cloud Run; Kubernetes-level control is GKE, and Autopilot is Google's recommendation unless you need privileges or configuration it disallows. Use Compute Engine only for lift-and-shift, custom OS, VM-bound licensing or special hardware. Use Spot for fault-tolerant, checkpointed batch and CUDs only for the steady baseline, never for peak capacity.

takeaways.title: Choose the database and storage from consistency, scale and access pattern
takeaways.body: Global, strongly consistent relational with horizontal write scale is Spanner; regional MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server is Cloud SQL; key-based wide-column throughput and time series is Bigtable; shared POSIX across VMs and GKE is Filestore. Cloud Storage cold classes differ in price and minimum duration (30, 90, 365 days), not latency, so rarely read multi-year data belongs in Archive with a lifecycle rule.

takeaways.title: Pick the private-connectivity tool by IP overlap and direction
takeaways.body: Private Service Connect reaches a producer service or Google API through an internal endpoint and tolerates overlapping ranges; VPC Peering needs non-overlapping ranges and is not transitive; Cloud NAT is outbound-only. For global users, a global external Application Load Balancer gives one anycast IP and nearest-healthy-backend routing, with Cloud CDN for cacheable content. Use HA VPN to start quickly and Interconnect for sustained bandwidth and low latency.

takeaways.title: Assess before you migrate, and match strategy and tooling to the workload
takeaways.body: Run discovery, dependency mapping and TCO in Migration Center first, move dependent apps in the same wave, and start with low-dependency workloads. Retire duplicated or unneeded apps, rehost for tight deadlines, and reserve refactor or rebuild for apps where agility pays. Use continuous Database Migration Service jobs for low-downtime cutover, Transfer Appliance when upload would take over a week, and sole-tenant nodes when BYOL requires dedicated hardware.
